headline: ⚠️ READ THE TIMESTAMP FIRST — THIS BOARD IS NOW FROZEN AT SUNDAY EVENING, ABOUT TWENTY-NINE HOURS BACK, AND IT IS NOT PRETENDING OTHERWISE. ShowingTime mail is this board's only source and the mail system has been absent from every refresh since 11:41 this morning, so no showing, no cancellation and no feedback form from today has been read. Nothing below is a claim that today was quiet — it is a statement that today was not looked at. ✅ TWO THINGS DID CHANGE AND BOTH CAME FROM VERIFIED NON-MAIL SOURCES: the 5167 Lake Crest closing date is SETTLED at Thursday 8/20 with the extension signed Saturday, so it is no longer printed as contested; and the 2–3 PM tour on 2368 Ridge Trail has come and gone with nobody watching, which makes it the single best follow-up call on this board tomorrow morning. 🔴 THE MOST ACTIONABLE THING HERE HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH THE OUTAGE: 'Publish to Seller' is still unclicked on all three 821 Martinwood feedback forms, so your seller cannot see the buyer's agent who came back VERY interested on Saturday. That is two clicks, and it has been four days.

hotSignals.signal: Wanda W. at Millennium Homes answered "interested: VERY" off Saturday's 12:50 PM showing — the first feedback this listing has produced in the whole window, and the only unqualified interest on the board that is less than a day old. ⚠️ She filed a second form ninety seconds later on a DIFFERENT buyer from Sunday's 3:00 PM showing that reads "not interested" — two buyers, two answers, same agent. ⛔ Every other field on both forms is blank: no price opinion, no rating, no comments. She has told us someone wants it and nothing about why.
hotSignals.action: 🔴 TWO MOVES, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE ONE BEING MISSED. (1) Call Wanda W. at Millennium Homes — thank her for the weekend, quote back what her buyer liked, and ask straight out what gets that buyer into the house; the seller is motivated. Never name a concession or a replacement price. (2) CLICK 'PUBLISH TO SELLER' ON ALL THREE FEEDBACK FORMS — it is unclicked on every one of them, so your seller has been shown none of this, including the very interested buyer. Four days of a seller sitting in silence on his own good news.

hotSignals.signal: Cassie C. at RE/MAX Advantage answered 'interested: Yes' and wrote "Writing up an offer!" on her form while calling $299,000 too high — that is the offer confirmed dead on Saturday morning, from a buyer who was never told the price came down to $295,000.
hotSignals.action: ⏰ CALL HER BEFORE 1:30 TODAY. There is a showing on this house this afternoon, and you want the agent who already wrote one offer to know the number moved before somebody else likes it, not after. Thank her for showing, tell her the number her client called too high is now $295,000, and ask what gets their buyer in the house. Quote $295,000 and nothing else. No email — a buyer's agent on a live listing is a call, not a message. ⚠️ Her written read has aged out of the 14-day window; the call task is live and the signal is carried here deliberately rather than dropped.

hotSignals.signal: Angela B. at Keller Williams Vestavia filed the listing's other 'interested: Yes', objecting only to the price at $299,000 and noting her buyer had seen another home she liked.
hotSignals.action: Call her — the price objection has already been answered by the reduction and she was never told. A week on, the cross-shopped house is either under contract or not, and one call settles it. Quote $295,000 only. ⏰ Her read ages out of the window in five days, so the written record of this yes is on a clock even though the call is not.

hotSignals.signal: Robert B. at RealtyCore asked at 2:35 Saturday whether Thursday worked for the inspection — and the inspector, Ron G., then reached you directly by text at 5:08. You answered at 5:30: Thursday 8/13, 11:15 AM, with the lockbox combo.
hotSignals.action: ✅ RESOLVED — the appointment is set. ⚠️ TWO LOOSE ENDS AND BOTH ARE YOURS. Your sellers have not been told that an inspector has their door code for Thursday, and there is no outbound to them anywhere since that text. And the buyer's agent — who asked the question in writing — still has nothing written back; the whole confirmation happened over text with a third party. One call to the sellers, one line to the agent.

hotSignals.signal: Mallory W. at ARC Realty filed the only unqualified 'interested: Yes / priced just right' this board has ever taken — her buyer wants to write and is short on down payment, nothing else.
hotSignals.action: The agent call is cleared. The open item is the seller decision behind it — authorize a concession or hold at list — and one call covers this seller's three files.

upcoming: ⚠️ TODAY, ALREADY PAST · 2:00–3:00 PM — 2368 RIDGE TRAIL, Birmingham. 🔴 THE OUTCOME OF THIS IS UNKNOWN AND THAT IS THE POINT: it was the first booking on this listing since 8/4, confirmed Sunday evening by an ARC Realty agent, and the window passed during the outage with no system able to capture a confirmation, a cancellation or a feedback form. ⭐ TREAT IT AS PENDING, NOT DEAD — this is the best follow-up call on the board tomorrow morning, on the listing whose last read said the price was too high.

Whatever landed this afternoon is sitting unread, not absent.

🔍 THU 8/13 · 11:15 AM — 1709 FIELDSTONE CIR inspection. ✅ CONFIRMED ON BOTH SIDES AND IN WRITING WITH THE SELLERS: you emailed Dennis and Leigh at 6:52 AM and Dennis replied 'That'll work' an hour later. This is the one item on the board that needs nothing from you.

📅 THU 8/20 · 5167 LAKE CREST CIR closing at the law firm. ✅ THE DATE IS NOW SETTLED AND THIS ENTRY HAS BEEN CORRECTED — it was printed as contested for two days and it is not contested any more: the extension was signed Saturday and 8/20 is the real date. 🔴 THE REMAINING JOB IS INTERNAL: your own brokerage has emailed the fourteenth three times and generated the commission document against that wrong date. Roughly three clicks, plus the commission document that was never actioned — and August's coverage rides on this file.

🚫 CANCELLED SUNDAY · 198 RENA DR 4:30 PM — requested, confirmed and cancelled inside a hundred minutes. ⭐ THE CANCELLATION WAS ILLNESS, NOT THE HOUSE, verified and closed out. Carry that into the seller call: it is traffic at the current price on day eighty-three, and it should never be handed to them as market rejection.
⭐ ALSO WORTH KNOWING: a teammate's buyer asked to see 355 Comanche and is working on pre-approval. Not booked in the system, so it will not appear here until it is.

That is a cross-shopping buyer, not a rejection — and her price objection was answered three days later by the cut to $295,000, which she was never told about. ⚠️ Like every other agent on this file, she left 'what price' blank. ⏳ This read ages out of the window Friday.

🔥 NOT A FEEDBACK FORM — A DEAL. 🔥 WROTE THE OFFER. Contract, pre-approval letter and a personal letter from the buyers, submitted 3:15 PM, followed by his own text eleven minutes later.

Ask him on the call; a single unanswered notice is not evidence of an unsigned document. 🆕 AND ONE FOUND THIS MORNING: your CRM has this listing marked EXPIRED while it is under contract with a Thursday inspection — a data problem, not a deal problem, but it stops feeding every downstream system.

Eighty-three days on market with one offer is the context that call needs.

oweFeedback.when: 🔴 ASKED THREE TIMES — Thu 7/30, Fri 7/31, Sat 8/1 — from the Keller Williams Realty Hoover listing side after your 7/30 tour, and you have since CLOSED on the property AND BEEN PAID. ⭐ STILL THE MOST OVERDUE ITEM ON THE BOARD in relationship terms, and getting paid sharpened it. Before the closing it read as an oversight; after completing a deal together and collecting on it, it reads as a shrug at the agent across the table. ⚠️ Their last request is now eight days old and their listing has gone EXPIRED, so the window where feedback is still useful to them has all but shut. Thirty seconds, and the same message carries the two answers you actually want back.
